instruction.text: This is Mary, a passenger on the Titanic. Select her to find out what she thinks about the ship.

atoms.sound: Wow, there’s so many people here!

feedback.finish: There were 2,200 people onboard the Titanic when it set sail from Southampton.

instruction.text: Let’s talk more to Mary. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Can you tell me about the different types of ((++people donkeys)) on the Titanic?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>Can you tell me about the different types of people on the Titanic?</prosody>

atoms.b: There are three ((++different identical)) classes of people on the Titanic.
The class that you are in is based on how much ((++money food)) you paid for the ticket.
What kind of ((++jobs pets)) do the people in each class have?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>What kind of jobs do the people in each class have?</prosody>

atoms.b: The first class passengers are mostly ((++rich funny)) businessmen. Most of the ((++second smelly)) class passengers are tourists. They have jobs like teaching or being a vicar.
What about the ((++third fiftieth)) class passengers?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>What about the third class passengers?</prosody>

atoms.b: Most third class passengers are ((++poor pink)) people who want to start a new life in ((++America France)).
Wow, it sounds like the Titanic was full of ((++interesting similar)) people!
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-0.5st'>Wow, it sounds like the Titanic was full of interesting people!</prosody>

instruction.text: Sort the Titanic tickets from most expensive at the top to least expensive at the bottom.

feedback.finish: Exactly! The first class tickets were the most expensive. In today’s money, it would cost around £800!

instruction.text: Match the image to the part of the ship that only first class passengers were allowed to use.
Select this third class passenger to find out about his experience on the Titanic before it sank.

atoms.sound: We have to share our rooms with ten people, and there are only two baths between all 700 of us!

instruction.text: Listen to the statements and decide which one is true.

b.sound: The third class passengers had a worse experience than the other passengers.
The third class passengers had the best experience on the Titanic.

feedback.finish: The first and second class passengers had a much better experience onboard the Titanic. They were also more likely to be saved when it sank.
